reports.scope: Same fwp Rosenbrock objective and reverse-mode gradient, input and step size. History stores N values including the initial point, so both execute N-1 updates. Loop keeps only current weights. Raw interpreters and native outputs match exactly; an independent analytic derivative is checked with relative/absolute tolerance 1e-10. This is a program-structure comparison, not a compiler improvement or C/Rust overhead. Timings include fresh-process startup, calculation, printing and teardown. Compilation, raw interpretation and separate managed profiles are excluded. Managed profiles and raw numeric derivative storage are separate ledgers. Raw profiles track actual successful allocator requests and frees for registry, parents, local derivatives and backward adjoints, including retained workspace. They exclude allocator metadata, temporary realloc copies and stack storage. Per-kind peaks need not coincide; do not add them to obtain a process peak. Separate uninstrumented GNU-time runs report process peak RSS. Timings explicitly enable workspace reuse; extra untimed profiles disable it. Idle raw storage must be constant after each selected backward pass and zero after actual shutdown. The finite repeated cases stay below tape-generation exhaustion and do not establish bounds for arbitrary nesting or run lengths. All timing samples are retained; no elapsed-time budget is set.
